rationale.Physical Exam: Chest / Lungs: Monitor respiratory muscle function — FVC, NIF.
rationale.Physical Exam: Neuro / Psych: Symmetric ascending weakness, areflexia, paresthesias. Facial diplegia possible. Sensation often preserved.

hpi: {{patient_name}} presents with rapidly progressive symmetric ascending weakness beginning in the lower extremities, areflexia, and possible paresthesias. History often reveals antecedent infection (Campylobacter jejuni most common, also viral URI, EBV, CMV) or vaccination within 1-4 weeks. GBS is an acute inflammatory demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy (AIDP) caused by molecular mimicry — antibodies against infectious agents cross-react with peripheral nerve antigens. Classic: ascending symmetric weakness + areflexia + albuminocytologic dissociation in CSF (elevated protein with normal WBC count). EMG/NCS shows demyelinating pattern. Critical complication: respiratory failure from diaphragm involvement — monitor FVC and NIF (negative inspiratory force). FVC <20 mL/kg or NIF <-30 cm H2O = elective intubation. Autonomic instability common (labile BP, arrhythmias). Treatment: IVIG (0.4g/kg/day x 5 days) or plasmapheresis — both equally effective. Do NOT give steroids (ineffective in GBS, unlike CIDP). ICU admission for monitoring. Prognosis: 85% recover, 3-5% mortality.
